assertion.text: Erdős Problem #450: declared status 'open'. Formalized: no. How large must $y=y(\epsilon,n)$ be such that the number of integers in $(x,x+y)$ with a divisor in $(n,2n)$ is at most $\epsilon y$? Current best: On the other hand, Cambie has observed that if $\epsilon\ll 1/n$ then $y(\epsilon,n)\sim 2n$: indeed, if $y<2n$ then this is impossible taking $x+n$ to be a multiple of the lowest common multiple of $\{n+1,\ldots,2n-1\}$. Prize: no. Tags: divisors, number theory.
